<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Allowance for Credit Losses on Off-Balance Sheet Credit Exposures</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae45" continuedAt="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae46"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9106" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9107">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae46" continuedAt="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae47"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9107" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9108">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company estimates expected credit losses over the contractual period in which the Company has exposure to credit risk via a contractual
      obligation to extend credit, unless that obligation is unconditionally cancellable by the Company. The allowance for credit losses on off-balance sheet credit exposures is adjusted as an expense in other noninterest expense. The estimate includes
      consideration of the likelihood that funding will occur and an estimate of expected credit losses on commitments expected to be funded over their estimated lives. Estimating credit losses on unfunded commitments requires the Bank to consider the
      following categories of off-balance sheet credit exposure: unfunded commitments to extend credit, unfunded lines of credit and standby letters of credit. Each of these unfunded commitments is then analyzed for a probability of funding to calculate a
      probable funding amount. The life of loan loss factor by related portfolio segment from the loan allowance for credit loss calculation is then applied to the probable funding amount to calculate a reserve on unfunded commitments.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae47" continuedAt="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae48"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9108" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9109">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae48" continuedAt="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae49"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9109" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9110">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Accrued Interest Receivable</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae49" continuedAt="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae50"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9110" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9111">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d6901663ec384cd4aa59a2892b1acfae50"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9111" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9112">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Accrued interest receivable (&#8220;AIR&#8221;) balances are included in other assets on the consolidated balance sheets. The Company has excluded interest
      receivable that is included in amortized cost of financing receivables from related disclosure requirements and AIR is written off by reversing interest income. For loans, write off typically occurs upon becoming over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:ThresholdPeriodPastDueForLoansToBeWrittenOff" id="Fact_5a33d3c8e03745ee931f12ae2cd82006" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:ThresholdPeriodPastDueForLoansToBeWrittenOff" id="Fact_906fd71247db46f287734163720119bc" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durday">120</ix:nonNumeric> days past due and therefore the
      amount of such write offs are immaterial. Historically, the Company has not experienced uncollectible AIR on investment securities.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9112" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9113">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Premises and Equipment</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ff8d5fc8c5d746e39bf7563bbab8f3361" continuedAt="Text_ff8d5fc8c5d746e39bf7563bbab8f3362"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9114" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9115">
<div><br/>

</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ff8d5fc8c5d746e39bf7563bbab8f3362"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9115" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9116">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Premises and equipment are stated at cost, less accumulated depreciation.&#160;Depreciation of premises and equipment is determined using the straight-line method over the
      estimated useful lives of the respective assets. Expenditures for maintenance, repairs and minor replacements are charged to expense as incurred.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Leases</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade1" continuedAt="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade2"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9118" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9119">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade2" continuedAt="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade3"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9119" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9120">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company determines if a lease is present at the inception of an agreement. Right-of-use (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) assets and lease liabilities are recognized at lease commencement
      based on the present value of the remaining lease payments using a discount rate that represents the Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate at the lease commencement date. ROU assets and operating lease liabilities, are included in other assets and
      other liabilities, respectively, on the <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">consolidated balance sheets</span>. Leases with original terms of 12 months or less are recognized in profit or loss on a
      straight-line basis over the lease term.</div>

    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade4" continuedAt="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade5"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9121" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9122">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Operating lease ROU assets represent the Company&#8217;s right to use an underlying asset during the lease term and operating lease liabilities represent our obligation to
      make lease payments arising from the lease. ROU assets are further adjusted for lease incentives. Operating lease expense, which is comprised of amortization of the ROU asset and the implicit interest accreted on the operating lease liability, is
      recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term, and is recorded in occupancy expense in the <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">consolidated statements of income</span>.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade5" continuedAt="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade6"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9122" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9123">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0bf0699de680443a82befa5466173ade6"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9123" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9124">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has lease agreements with lease and non-lease components, which are generally accounted for separately. For real estate leases, non-lease components and
      other non-components, such as common area maintenance charges, real estate taxes and insurance are not included in the measurement of the lease liability since they are generally able to be segregated. Our leases relate primarily to office space and
      bank branches, and some contain options to renew the lease. These options to renew are generally not considered reasonably certain to exercise, and are therefore not included in the lease term until such time that the option to renew is reasonably
      certain.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9124" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9125">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableRealEstateAcquiredThroughForeclosurePolicy" id="Text_38da0f82327b437c820480eb47d72f35" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_b94ea49bde734c218776c33aab20b0b21"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9125" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9126">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Other Real Estate Owned</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_b94ea49bde734c218776c33aab20b0b21" continuedAt="Text_b94ea49bde734c218776c33aab20b0b22"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9126" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9127">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_b94ea49bde734c218776c33aab20b0b22"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9127" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9128">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) consists of properties acquired through foreclosure or by acceptance of a deed in lieu of foreclosure. These assets are recorded at the
      lower of fair value of the asset acquired less estimated costs to sell or &#8220;cost&#8221; (defined as the fair value at initial foreclosure). At the time of foreclosure, or when foreclosure occurs in-substance, any excess loan balance over fair market value
      of the acquired asset, less estimated selling costs, is charged to the allowance for loan losses. Any subsequent valuation write-downs are recorded as other expense. In connection with the determination of the allowance for loan losses and the
      valuation of OREO, management obtains appraisals for properties. Operating costs associated with the properties are expensed as incurred. Gains on the sale of OREO are recognized as income when title has passed and the sale has met the minimum down
      payment requirements prescribed by GAAP. The balance of OREO is recorded in other assets on the consolidated balance sheets.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9128" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9129">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsIntangibleAssetsPolicy" id="Text_6d9aeaf638944bf5be57b3f496179cbc" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a1"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9129" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9130">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a1" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a2"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9130" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9131">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a2" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a3"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9131" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9132">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Goodwill represents the cost of acquired business in excess of the fair value of the related net assets acquired. Goodwill is not amortized but tested at the reporting
      unit level for impairment on an annual basis and on an interim basis or when events or circumstances dictate. The Company has elected June 30 as the annual impairment testing date for the insurance and retirement services reporting units and December
      31 for the Bank reporting unit.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a3" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a4"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9132" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9133">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a4" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a5"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9133" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9134">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has the option to first assess qualitative factors, by performing a qualitative analysis, to determine whether the existence of events or circumstances leads
      to a determination that it is more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. If, after assessing the events or circumstances, the Company determines it is more likely than not that the fair value of a
      reporting unit is greater than its carrying amount, the impairment test is not required. If the Company concludes otherwise, the Company is required to perform a quantitative impairment test. In the quantitative impairment test, the estimated fair
      value of a reporting unit is compared to the carrying amount in order to determine if impairment is indicated. If the estimated fair value exceeds the carrying amount, the reporting unit is not deemed to be impaired. If the estimated fair value is
      below the carrying value of the reporting unit, the difference is the amount of impairment.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a5" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a6"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9134" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9135">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a6" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a7"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9135" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9136">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Intangible assets that have indefinite useful lives are not amortized, but are tested at least annually for impairment. Intangible assets that have finite useful lives
      are amortized over their useful lives.&#160;Core deposit intangibles and trust intangibles at the Company are amortized using the sum-of-the-years&#8217;-digits method.&#160;Covenants not to compete are amortized on a straight-line basis.&#160;Customer lists are
      amortized using an accelerated method. When facts and circumstances indicate potential impairment of amortizable intangible assets, the Company evaluates the recoverability of the asset carrying value, using estimates of undiscounted future cash
      flows over the remaining asset life. Any impairment loss is measured by the excess of carrying value over fair value.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a7" continuedAt="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a8"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9136" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9137">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_947986bfeeaf467cb6deb4516ffe665a8"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9137" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9138">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Determining the fair value of a reporting unit under the goodwill impairment tests and determining the fair value of other intangible assets are judgmental and often
      involve the use of significant estimates and assumptions. Estimates of fair value are primarily determined using the discounted cash flows method, which uses significant estimates and assumptions including projected future cash flows, discount rates
      reflecting the market rate of return and projected growth rates. Future events may impact such estimates and assumptions and could cause the Company to conclude that our goodwill or intangible assets have become impaired, which would result in
      recording an impairment loss.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9138" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9139">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:BankOwnedLifeInsurancePolicyTextBlock" id="Text_5463296bf63e4104b7e9a16dffc31863" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_aa98d0ea72514be68a607809f3efdc111"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9139" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9140">

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank has purchased life insurance policies on certain employees, key executives and directors. Bank owned life insurance is recorded at the amount that can be
      realized under the insurance contract at the balance sheet date, which is the cash surrender value adjusted for other charges or other amounts due that are probable at settlement.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Treasury Stock</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_b62968e7db734ee785e1cf28b7b662f41" continuedAt="Text_b62968e7db734ee785e1cf28b7b662f42"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9144" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9145">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_b62968e7db734ee785e1cf28b7b662f42"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9145" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9146">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Treasury stock acquisitions are recorded at cost. Subsequent sales of treasury stock are recorded on an average cost basis. Gains on the sale of treasury stock are
      credited to additional paid-in-capital. Losses on the sale of treasury stock are charged to additional paid-in-capital to the extent of previous gains, otherwise charged to retained earnings.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_d11b512da52c414b842023f5b3dca452" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6561"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9147" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9148">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Income Taxes</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6561" continuedAt="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6562"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9148" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9149">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6562" continuedAt="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6563"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9149" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9150">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method. Deferred income taxes are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences
      between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases.&#160;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which
      those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred taxes of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date. A valuation allowance, if needed, reduces deferred tax
      assets to the amount expected to be realized. The realization of deferred tax assets is primarily dependent upon the generation of adequate future taxable income. The Company recognizes interest accrued and penalties related to unrecognized tax
      benefits in income tax expense.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6563" continuedAt="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6564"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9150" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9151">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_58a7a72593e54aa59edde9a0f49ee6564"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9151" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9152">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Tax positions are recognized as a benefit only if it is &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; that the tax position would be sustained in a tax examination, with a tax examination
      being presumed to occur. The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50 percent likely of being realized on examination. For tax positions not meeting the &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; test, no tax benefit is recorded.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9152" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9153">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_2c31bb63f17148ae8c9523f8eba94e1b2"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9159" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9160">

    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10eda5b8bd05413cb6ad9997b51f9cbd2"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9163" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9164">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Basic earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) excludes dilution and is computed by dividing income available to common stockholders by the weighted average number of common shares
      outstanding for the period. Diluted EPS reflects the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock or resulted in the issuance of common stock that then shared
      in the earnings of the entity (such as the Company&#8217;s dilutive restricted stock units and stock options).</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9164" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9165">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_42916449ccca45f4bfbbe19122b5d3fa" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_f017bd5a87dd4a1a83c4c3c244216eb71"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9165" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9166">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Comprehensive Income (Loss)<br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_f017bd5a87dd4a1a83c4c3c244216eb71" continuedAt="Text_f017bd5a87dd4a1a83c4c3c244216eb72"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9166" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9167">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_f017bd5a87dd4a1a83c4c3c244216eb72"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9167" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9168">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At the Company, comprehensive income (loss) represents net income plus OCI, which consists primarily of the net change in unrealized gains (losses) on AFS debt
      securities for the period, changes in the funded status of employee benefit plans and unrealized gains (losses) on derivatives designated as hedging instruments. AOCI represents the net unrealized gains (losses) on AFS debt securities, the previously
      unrecognized portion of the funded status of employee benefit plans and the fair value of instruments designated as hedging instruments, net of income taxes, as of the consolidated balance sheet dates.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9168" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9169">
<div style="text-align: left;"><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_cb82ff9b1e624e6a97cf75c24f405c4b" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f151"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9169" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9170">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f151" continuedAt="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f152"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9170" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9171">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f152" continuedAt="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f153"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9171" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9172">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company records all derivatives on the consolidated balance sheet at fair value.&#160;The accounting for changes in the fair value of derivatives depends on the intended
      use of the derivative, whether the Company has elected to designate a derivative in a hedging relationship and apply hedge accounting and whether the hedging relationship has satisfied the criteria necessary to apply hedge accounting. Derivatives
      designated and qualifying as a hedge of the exposure to changes in the fair value of an asset, liability or firm commitment attributable to a particular risk, such as interest rate risk, are considered fair value hedges. Derivatives designated and
      qualifying as a hedge of the exposure to variability in expected future cash flows, or other types of forecasted transactions, are considered cash flow hedges. Hedge accounting generally provides for the matching of the timing of gain or loss
      recognition on the hedging instrument with the recognition of the changes in the fair value of the hedged asset or liability that are attributable to the hedged risk in a fair value hedge or the earnings effect of the hedged forecasted transactions
      in a cash flow hedge. The Company may enter into derivative contracts that are intended to economically hedge certain of its risks, even though hedge accounting does not apply or the Company elects not to apply hedge accounting.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f153" continuedAt="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f154"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9172" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9173">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f154" continuedAt="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f155"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9173" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9174">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">For derivatives designated as fair value hedges, changes in the fair value of the derivative and the hedged item related to the hedged risk are
      recognized in earnings.<br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f155" continuedAt="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f156"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9174" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9175">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_491d81bf7c09455895c568e3bcb24f156"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9175" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9176">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">When the Company purchases or sells a portion of a commercial loan that has an existing interest rate swap, it may enter into a risk participation agreement <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">to provide credit protection to the financial institution that originated the swap transaction should the borrower fail to perform on its obligation. The Company enters
        into both risk participation agreements in which it purchases credit protection from other financial institutions and those in which it provides credit protection to other financial institutions</span>. Any fee paid to the Company under a risk
      participation agreement is in consideration of the credit risk of the counterparties and is recognized in the income statement. Credit risk on the risk participation agreements is determined after considering the risk rating, PD and LGD of the
      counterparties.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9176" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9177">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationsPolicy" id="Text_c1e7968b06fe4ed08b0de1e69e5fc33e" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c01"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9177" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9178">
<div style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Business Combinations</span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c01" continuedAt="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c02"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9178" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9179">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c02" continuedAt="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c03"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9179" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9180">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-weight: bold;"> <br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c03" continuedAt="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c04"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9180" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9181">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_80804d6563084766ae1bfab0a93366c04"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9181" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9182">
<div style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-weight: bold;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-weight: normal;">Business




































































            combinations are accounted for under the acquisition method of accounting. Acquired assets, including separately identifiable intangible assets, and assumed liabilities are recorded at their acquisition date estimated fair values. The excess of
            the cost of acquisition over these fair values is recognized as goodwill. During the measurement period, which cannot exceed one year from the acquisition date, changes to estimated fair values are recognized as an adjustment to goodwill.
            Certain transaction costs are expensed as incurred. See Note 3 for additional information.</span></span><br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <div style="text-align: justify;"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9182" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9183">

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_0912e0c6f5a14d37bc891040eaf3d125" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f1"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9183" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9184">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Fair Value Measurements</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f1" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f2"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9184" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9185">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f2" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f3"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9185" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9186">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">GAAP states that fair value is an exit price, representing the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction
      between market participants. Fair value measurements are not adjusted for transaction costs.&#160;A fair value hierarchy exists within GAAP that prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest
      priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3 measurements). The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are described below:</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f3" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f4"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9186" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9187">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f4" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f5"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9187" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9188">
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-weight: normal; text-align: justify;"> Level 1 - Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted
      assets or liabilities; </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f5" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f6"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9188" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9189">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f6" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f7"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9189" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9190">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 2 -&#160;Quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are not active or inputs that are observable, either directly
      or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset or liability; and<br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f7" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f8"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9190" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9191">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f8" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f9"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9191" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9192">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 3 - Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable (i.e., supported by little or no
      market activity).</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f9" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f10"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9192" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9193">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f10" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f11"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9193" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9194">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A financial instrument&#8217;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f11" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f12"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9194" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9195">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f12" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f13"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9195" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9196">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The types of instruments valued based on quoted market prices in active markets include most U.S. government and agency securities, many other sovereign government
      obligations, liquid mortgage products, active listed equities and most money market securities. Such instruments are generally classified within Level 1 or Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy. The Company does not adjust the quoted prices for such
      instruments.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f13" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f14"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9196" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9197">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f14" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f15"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9197" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9198">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The types of instruments valued based on quoted prices in markets that are not active, broker or dealer quotations or quote from alternative pricing sources with
      reasonable levels of price transparency include most investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds, less liquid mortgage products, less liquid agency securities, less liquid listed equities, state, municipal and provincial obligations and certain
      physical commodities. Such instruments are generally classified within Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy. Certain common equity securities are reported at fair value utilizing Level 1 inputs (exchange quoted prices). Other investment securities are
      reported at fair value utilizing Level 1 and Level 2 inputs. The prices for Level 2 instruments are obtained through an independent pricing service or dealer market participants with whom the Company has historically transacted both purchases and
      sales of investment securities. Prices obtained from these sources include prices derived from market quotations and matrix pricing. The fair value measurements consider observable data that may include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash flows, the
      U.S. Treasury yield curve, live trading levels, trade execution data, market consensus prepayment speeds, credit information and the bond&#8217;s terms and conditions, among other things. Management reviews the methodologies used&#160; by its third-party
      providers in pricing the securities.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f15" continuedAt="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f16"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9198" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9199">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ba1f637cea72426aafeba7c2be63ae5f16"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9199" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9200">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 3 is for positions that are not traded in active markets or are subject to transfer restrictions. Valuations are adjusted to reflect illiquidity and/or
      non-transferability and such adjustments are generally based on available market evidence. In the absence of such evidence, management&#8217;s best estimate will be used. Management&#8217;s best estimate consists of both internal and external support on certain
      Level 3 investments. Subsequent to inception, management only changes Level 3 inputs and assumptions when corroborated by evidence such as transactions in similar instruments, completed or pending third-party transactions in the underlying investment
      or comparable entities, subsequent rounds of financing, recapitalizations and other transactions across the capital structure, offerings in the equity or debt markets and changes in financial ratios or cash flows.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9200" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9201">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Other Financial Instruments</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca771" continuedAt="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca772"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9202" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9203">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca772" continuedAt="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca773"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9203" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9204">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is a party to certain financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These
      financial instruments include commitments to extend credit, unused lines of credit, standby letter of credit and certain agricultural real estate loans sold to investors with recourse, with the sold portion having a government guarantee that is
      assignable back to the Company upon repurchase of the loan in the event of default. The Company&#8217;s policy is to record such instruments when funded.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca773" continuedAt="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca774"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9204" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9205">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_52976e3e843f4c4d935c5992c3f1ca774"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9205" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9206">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued to guarantee the performance of a customer to a third-party. The risk involved in issuing standby letters of
      credit is essentially the same as the credit risk involved in extending loan facilities to customers and letters of credit are subject to the same credit origination, portfolio maintenance and management procedures in effect to monitor other credit
      and off-balance sheet products. Under the standby letters of credit, the Company is required to make payments to the beneficiary of the letters of credit upon request by the beneficiary contingent upon the customer&#8217;s failure to perform under the
      terms of the underlying contract with the beneficiary. Standby letters of credit typically have <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:StandbyLettersOfCreditExpirationPeriod" id="Fact_189d7d8c49954a78890e3de5e00c3d42" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one-year</ix:nonNumeric> expiration terms with an option
      to renew upon annual review. The Company typically receives a fee for these transactions. The fair value of standby letters of credit is recorded upon inception.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9206" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9207">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RepurchaseAndResaleAgreementsPolicy" id="Text_906fd7c93e64406facabce637172d6f4" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_7717bd0fb0824678ad1a6e5beebbaeb21"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9207" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9208">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Repurchase Agreements</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_7717bd0fb0824678ad1a6e5beebbaeb21" continuedAt="Text_7717bd0fb0824678ad1a6e5beebbaeb22"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9208" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9209">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_7717bd0fb0824678ad1a6e5beebbaeb22"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9209" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9210">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Repurchase agreements are accounted for as secured financing transactions since the Company maintains effective control over the transferred
      securities and the transfer meets the other criteria for such accounting.&#160;Obligations to repurchase securities sold are reflected as a liability in the consolidated balance sheets.&#160;The securities underlying the agreements are delivered to a custodial
      account for the benefit of the counterparties with whom each transaction is executed.&#160;The counterparties, who may sell, loan or otherwise dispose of such securities to other parties in the normal course of their operations, agree to resell to the
      Company the same securities at the maturities of the agreements.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9210" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9211">

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_bc77d5aea6744cba9290032e426cdb1a" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745761"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9211" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9212">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745761" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745762"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9212" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9213">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745762" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745763"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9213" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9214">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with ASU 2014-09, <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Revenue






































































        from Contracts with Customers</span>&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">(Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic 606) </span>(&#8220;ASC 606&#8221;), and all subsequent ASUs that modified ASC 606. ASC
      606 does not apply to revenue associated with financial instruments, including revenue from loans and securities and certain noninterest income streams such as fees associated with mortgage servicing rights, financial guarantees, derivatives and
      certain credit card fees are also not in scope. ASC 606 is applicable to noninterest revenue streams such as retirement plan administration fees, trust and asset management income, deposit related fees and annuity and insurance commissions.
      Noninterest revenue streams in-scope of ASC 606 are discussed below.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745763" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745764"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9214" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9215">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745764" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745765"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9215" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9216">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Service Charges on Deposit Accounts </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745765" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745766"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9216" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9217">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745766" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745767"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9217" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9218">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Service charges on deposit accounts consist of overdraft fees, monthly service fees, check orders and other deposit account related fees. Overdraft, monthly service,
      check orders and other deposit account related fees are transactional based, and therefore, the Company&#8217;s performance obligation is satisfied, and related revenue recognized, at a point in time. Payment for service charges on deposit accounts is
      primarily received immediately or in the following month through a direct charge to customers&#8217; accounts.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745767" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745768"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9218" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9219">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745768" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745769"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9219" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9220">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Card Services Income<br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d49745769" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457610"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9220" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9221">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457610" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457611"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9221" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9222">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">ATM fees are primarily generated when a Company cardholder uses a non-Company ATM or a non-Company cardholder uses a Company ATM. Debit card income is primarily
      comprised of interchange fees earned whenever the Company&#8217;s debit cards are processed through card payment networks. The Company&#8217;s performance obligations for these revenue streams are satisfied, and related revenue recognized, when the services are
      rendered or upon completion. Payment is typically received immediately or in the following month.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457611" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457612"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9222" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9223">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457612" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457613"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9223" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9224">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Retirement Plan Administration Fees</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457613" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457614"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9224" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9225">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457614" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457615"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9225" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9226">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Retirement plan administration fees are primarily generated for services related to the recordkeeping, administration and plan design solutions of defined benefit,
      defined contribution and revenue sharing plans. Revenue is recognized in arrears for services already provided in accordance with fees established in contracts with customers or based on rates agreed to with investment trade platforms based on ending
      investment balances held. The Company&#8217;s performance obligation is satisfied, and related revenue recognized based on services completed or ending investment balances, for which receivables are recorded at the time of revenue recognition.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457615" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457616"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9226" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9227">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457616" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457617"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9227" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9228">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Wealth Management</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457617" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457618"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9228" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9229">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457618" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457619"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9229" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9230">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Wealth Management revenue primarily is comprised of trust and other financial services revenue. Trust and asset management income is primarily
      comprised of fees earned from the management and administration of trusts, pensions and other customer assets. The Company&#8217;s performance obligation is generally satisfied with the resulting fees recognized monthly, based upon services completed or
      the month-end market value of the assets under management and the applicable fee rate. Payment is generally received shortly after services are rendered or a few days after month end through a direct charge to customers&#8217; accounts. The Company does
      not earn performance-based incentives. Financial services revenue primarily consists of commissions received on brokered investment product sales. For other financial services revenue, the Company&#8217;s performance obligation is generally satisfied upon
      the issuance of the annuity policy. Shortly after the policy is issued, the carrier remits the commission payment to the Company, and the Company recognizes the revenue. The Company does not earn a significant amount of trailing commission fees on
      brokered investment product sales. The majority of the trailing commission fees are calculated based on a percentage of market value of a period end and revenue is recognized when an investment product&#8217;s market value can be determined.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457619" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457620"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9230" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9231">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457620" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457621"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9231" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9232">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Insurance Revenue</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457621" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457622"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9232" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9233">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457622" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457623"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9233" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9234">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Insurance and other financial services revenue primarily consists of commissions received on insurance. The Company acts as an intermediary between
      the Company&#8217;s customer and the insurance carrier. The Company&#8217;s performance obligation related to insurance sales for both property and casualty insurance and employee benefit plans is generally satisfied upon the later of the issuance or effective
      date of the policy. The Company earns performance based incentives, commonly known as contingent payments, which usually are based on certain criteria established by the insurance carrier such as premium volume, growth and insured loss ratios.
      Contingent payments are accrued for based upon management&#8217;s expectations for the year. Commission expense associated with sales of insurance products is expensed as incurred. The Company does not earn a significant amount of trailing commission fees
      on insurance product sales. The majority of the trailing commission fees are calculated based on a percentage of market value of a period end and revenue is recognized when an investment product&#8217;s market value can be determined.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457623" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457624"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9234" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9235">

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Other noninterest income consists of other recurring revenue streams such as account and loan fees, interest rate swap fees, safe deposit box rental fees and other
      miscellaneous revenue streams. These revenue streams are primarily transactional based and payment is received immediately or in the following month, and therefore, the Company&#8217;s performance obligation is satisfied, and the related revenue is
      recognized, at a point in time.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Contract Balances</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457633" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457634"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9244" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9245">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457634" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457635"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9245" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9246">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A contract asset balance occurs when an entity performs a service for a customer before the customer pays consideration or before payment is due, which would result in
      contract receivables or assets, respectively. A contract liability balance is an entity&#8217;s obligation to transfer a service to a customer for which the entity has already received payment or for which payment is due from the customer. The Company&#8217;s
      noninterest revenue streams are largely based on transactional activity, or standard month-end revenue accruals such as asset management fees based on month-end market values. Consideration is often received immediately or shortly after the Company
      satisfies its performance obligation and revenue is recognized. The Company does not typically enter into long-term revenue contracts with customers, and therefore, does not experience significant contract balances.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457635" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457636"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9246" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9247">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457636" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457637"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9247" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9248">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Contract Acquisition Costs</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457637" continuedAt="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457638"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9248" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9249">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_9f49dc87aca045538c7f6491d497457638"><ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9249" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9250">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">ASC 606 requires the capitalization, and subsequently amortization into expense, of certain incremental costs of obtaining a contract with a customer if these costs are
      expected to be recovered. The incremental costs of obtaining a contract are those costs that an entity incurs to obtain a contract with a customer that it would not have incurred if the contract had not been obtained. The Company elected the
      practical expedient, which allows immediate expensing of contract acquisition costs when the asset that would have resulted from capitalizing these costs would have been amortized in one year or less, and did not capitalize any contract acquisition
      costs as of or during the year ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9250" continuedAt="Text_a7ec0910898049f1883000b52fbb0fe9251">

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Trust Operations</div>

      not assets of the Company.</div>

<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Recently Adopted Accounting Standards</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_512f936fa4e741c1ac8f401639a803971" continuedAt="Text_512f936fa4e741c1ac8f401639a803972"><ix:continuation id="Text_de14b476c0c2466a91c7c17a3c0307c54" continuedAt="Text_de14b476c0c2466a91c7c17a3c0307c55">

    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
      <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
        <div>
          <div>
            <ix:continuation id="Text_512f936fa4e741c1ac8f401639a803972" continuedAt="Text_512f936fa4e741c1ac8f401639a803973"><ix:continuation id="Text_de14b476c0c2466a91c7c17a3c0307c55" continuedAt="Text_de14b476c0c2466a91c7c17a3c0307c56">
<div style="background-color: #FFFFFF; margin: 0px 0px 0px; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; text-align: justify; text-transform: none;">In November
              2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-07, <span style="font-style: italic;">Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures,</span> to enhance reportable segment disclosure requirements by requiring annual and interim disclosure of incremental
              segment information. In addition, the amendments will enhance interim disclosure requirements, clarify circumstances in which an entity can disclose multiple segment measures of profit or loss, provide new segment disclosure requirements for
              entities with a single reportable segment and include other disclosure requirements. The amendments in this ASU are effective for the Company for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2023, and interim periods within fiscal years
              beginning after December 15, 2024, and early adoption is permitted. The Company adopted ASU 2023-07 on December 31, 2024 on a retrospective basis, and aside from meeting the new disclosure requirements, the adoption did not have a material
              impact on the consolidated financial statements. See Note 1 and Note 22 for additional information.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">In December 2023, the
          FASB issued ASU 2023-09, <span style="font-style: italic;">Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</span>, in response to requests from investors, lenders, creditors and other allocators of capital for enhanced income tax disclosures to support
          capital allocation decisions. The ASU requires enhanced disclosures primarily related to existing rate reconciliation and income taxes paid information to help investors better assess how the Company&#8217;s operations and related tax risks and tax
          planning and operational opportunities affect the Company&#8217;s tax rate and prospects for future cash flows. The ASU 2023-09 improves the transparency of income tax disclosures. The amendments in this ASU are effective for the Company on January 1,
          2025 and should be applied on a prospective basis. Retrospective application and early adoption are permitted. Aside from complying with the new disclosure requirements, the adoption is not expected to have a material impact on the consolidated
          financial statements.</div>

          2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, <span style="font-style: italic;">Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses,</span> that addresses
          longstanding investor requests for more information of expenses included in the expense captions presented on the face of the income statement. The ASU will require a tabular disclosure that disaggregates certain income statement expenses
          including employee compensation, depreciation and intangible asset amortization. In January 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-01, <span style="font-style: italic;">Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures
            (Subtopic 220-40): Clarifying the Effective Date,</span> which revises the effective date of ASU 2024-03. The ASU will become effective in the annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and early adoption is permitted. Aside
          from complying with the new disclosure requirements, the adoption is not expected to have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</div>

      Company, with the Company surviving the merger, for $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" id="Fact_cabdba2c9f0f42bbb629caef9a30fc76" contextRef="c20230811to20230811_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">161.7</ix:nonFraction> million in stock. The acquisition enhances
      the Company&#8217;s presence in Massachusetts&#8217; Berkshire county, and extends its footprint into New York&#8217;s Dutchess, Orange and Ulster counties and Connecticut&#8217;s Litchfield county. In connection with the acquisition, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" id="Fact_9821afcbbd0b41278b697d1e518e9f0d" contextRef="c20230811to20230811_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U002" decimals="-4" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4.32</ix:nonFraction> million shares of common stock and acquired approximately $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedAssets" id="Fact_4366380167ff4782a9ff0c91ec5c40a9" contextRef="c20230811_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-7" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.46</ix:nonFraction> billion of identifiable assets. Goodwill of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:Goodwill" id="Fact_52df9d67374845baafb4675ac17b3794" contextRef="c20230811_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">79.7</ix:nonFraction> million was recognized as a result of the merger
      and is not amortizable or deductible for tax purposes. During the fourth quarter of 2023, the Company revised the estimated fair value of premises and equipment, net and related deferred income taxes based upon receipt of land and building
      appraisals, which resulted in a $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:GoodwillPeriodIncreaseDecrease" id="Fact_66d6fca23661458786d1996c0e8bd068" contextRef="c20231001to20231231_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.7</ix:nonFraction> million increase in goodwill. The effects of the acquired assets and liabilities have been included in

      accounting. Accordingly, as of the date of the acquisition, the Company recorded the assets acquired, liabilities assumed and consideration paid at fair value based on management&#8217;s best estimates using information available at the date of the
      acquisition and these estimates are subject to adjustment based on updated information not available at the time of the acquisition. The amount of goodwill arising from the acquisition consists largely of the synergies and economies of scale expected

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">The following is a description of the valuation methodologies used to estimate the fair values of major categories of assets acquired and liabilities assumed. The Company used an independent valuation specialist
          to assist with the determination of fair values for certain acquired assets and assumed liabilities.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701824" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701825">

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Cash and due from banks</span> - The estimated fair value was determined to approximate the carrying amount of these assets.</span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701826" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701827">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
