      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701827" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701828">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Securities available for sale</span> - The estimated fair value of the investment portfolio was based on quoted market prices and dealer quotes. The investment securities were sold
          immediately after the merger and no gains or losses were recorded.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701828" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701829">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701829" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701830">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Loans</span> - The estimated fair value of loans were based on a discounted cash flow methodology applied on a pooled basis for</span> non-purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;non-PCD&#8221;) loans
        and for purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;PCD&#8221;) loans.<span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> The valuation
          considered underlying characteristics including loan type, term, rate, payment schedule and credit rating. Other factors included assumptions related to prepayments, PD and LGD. The discount rates applied were based on a build-up approach
          considering the funding mix, servicing costs, liquidity premium and factors related to performance risk.<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701830" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701831">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701831" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701832">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Core deposit intangible</span> - The core deposit intangible was valued utilizing the cost savings method approach, which recognizes the cost savings represented by the expense of
          maintaining the core deposit base versus the cost of an alternative funding source. The valuation incorporates assumptions related to account retention, discount rates, deposit interest rates, deposit maintenance costs and alternative funding
          rates.<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701832" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701833">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701833" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701834">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Wealth management customer intangible</span> - The wealth management customer intangible was valued utilizing the income approach, which employs a present value analysis, which
          calculates the expected after-tax cash flow benefits of the net revenues generated by the acquired customers over the expected lives of the acquired customers, discounted at a long-term market-oriented after-tax rate of return on investment. The
          value assigned to the acquired customers represents the future economic benefit from acquiring the customers (net of operating expenses).<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701834" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701835">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Deposits</span> - The fair value of noninterest bearing demand deposits, interest checking, money market and savings deposit accounts from Salisbury were assumed to approximate the
          carrying value as these accounts have no stated maturity and are payable on demand.</span> Certificate of deposit (&#8220;CD&#8221;)<span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> (time deposit accounts) were valued at the present value of the certificates&#8217; expected contractual payments discounted at market rates for similar certificates.<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701836" continuedAt="Text_15918e74462e4dc59f4514caaafc701837">

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Borrowings</span> - The estimated fair value of short-term borrowings was determined to approximate stated value. Subordinated debt was valued using a discounted cash flow approach
          incorporating a discount rate that incorporated similar terms, maturity and credit rating.<br/>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Accounting for Acquired Loans - </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Acquired














          loans are classified into two categories: PCD loans and non-PCD loans. PCD loans are defined as a loan or group of loans that have experienced more than insignificant credit deterioration since origination. Non-PCD loans had an allowance
          established on acquisition date, which was recognized as an expense through the provision for credit losses. For PCD loans, an allowance was recognized by adding it to the fair value of the loan, which is the amortized cost. There is no provision
          for credit loss expense recognized on PCD loans because the initial allowance is established by grossing-up the amortized cost of the PCD loan. The allowance for credit losses on non-PCD loans of $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:FinancingReceivablePurchasedWithoutCreditDeteriorationAllowanceForCreditLossAtAcquisitionDate" id="Fact_3bc620ad75bd4459a10d9b46729c3a8f" contextRef="c20230811to20230811_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">8.8</ix:nonFraction> million was recorded through the provision for loan losses within the unaudited interim consolidated statements of income.</span><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FairValueOfAcquiredPCDLoans" id="Text_510e5929cd824f10ba72e859be59dd46" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_57fd388f1d7e42ab94d8f8f664f526b31"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal;">The following table provides details related to the fair value of acquired PCD loans. </span></ix:nonNumeric></span> </div>

      securities. The Company does not intend to sell, nor is it more likely than not that the Company will be required to sell the securities before recovery of its amortized cost basis, which may be at maturity. The Company elected to exclude AIR from

<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance for credit losses calculation incorporated a 6-quarter forecast period to account for forecast economic conditions under each scenario
        utilized in the measurement. For periods beyond the 6-quarter forecast, the model reverts to long-term economic conditions over a 4-quarter reversion period on a straight-line basis. The Company considers a baseline, upside and downside economic
        forecast in measuring the allowance.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The quantitative model as of December 31, 2024 incorporated a baseline economic outlook along with an alternative downside scenario sourced from a
        reputable third-party to accommodate other potential economic conditions in the model. At December 31, 2024, the weightings were 80% and 20% for the baseline and downside economic forecasts, respectively. The baseline outlook reflected a Northeast
        unemployment rate environment starting at 4.1% and increasing slightly during the forecast period to 4.2%. Northeast Gross Domestic Product (&#8220;GDP&#8217;s&#8221;) annualized growth (on a quarterly basis) is expected to start the first quarter of 2025 at
        approximately 3.8% before decreasing to a low of 2.6% in the third quarter of 2025 and then increasing to 3.9% by the end of the forecast period. Key assumptions in the baseline economic outlook included <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">two 25 basis point federal funds rate cuts in 2025, quantitative tightening
          ending in early 2025, a post-election fiscal outlook with lower spending, lower taxes, and higher tariffs, and the economy currently being near full employment.</span> The alternative downside scenario assumed deteriorated economic conditions
        from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, Northeast unemployment increases to a peak of 7.5% in the first quarter of 2026. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated at each measurement date and reflect management&#8217;s
        expectations as of December 31, 2024. Additional qualitative adjustments were made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools, considerations for inflation and recent trends in
        asset value indices. Additional monitoring for industry concentrations, loan growth and policy exceptions was also conducted. </div>

        quarter of 2023 at approximately 3.9% and hovering around 4.6% by the end of the forecast period. Other utilized economic variables have generally deteriorated in their respective forecasts, with retail sales and housing starts forecasts declining
        from the prior year. Key assumptions in the baseline economic outlook included a full employment economy being realized in the near future, continued tapering of the Federal Reserve balance sheet, an increasing yield on ten-year treasury securities
        and a gradual decline in global oil prices. The alternative downside scenario assumed deteriorated economic and pandemic related conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, Northeast unemployment rises from 3.9% in the fourth quarter
        of 2022 to a peak of 6.9% in the first quarter of 2024. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated at each measurement date and reflect management&#8217;s expectations as of December 31, 2022. Additional qualitative adjustments were
        made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools, considerations for inflation and recent trends in asset value indices. Additional monitoring for industry concentrations, loan
        growth and policy exceptions was also conducted.</div>

      <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
        <div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
          <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73339" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73340"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e14" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e15">

            </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73340" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73341"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e15" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e16">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Credit Quality Indicators</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73341" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73342"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e16" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e17">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73342" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73343"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e17" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e18">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has developed an internal loan grading system to evaluate and quantify the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio with respect to quality and risk, focusing on, among
        other things, borrower&#8217;s financial strength, experience and depth of borrower&#8217;s management, primary and secondary sources of repayment, payment history, nature of the business and industry outlook. The internal grading system enables the Company to
        monitor the quality of the entire loan portfolio on a consistent basis and provide management with an early warning system, which facilitates recognition and response to problem loans and potential problem loans.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73343" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73344"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e18" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e19">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73344" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73345"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e19" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e20">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Commercial Grading System</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73345" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73346"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e20" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e21">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73346" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73347"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e21" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e22">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">For C&amp;I and CRE loans, the Company uses a grading system that relies on quantifiable and measurable characteristics when available. This includes comparison of
        financial strength to available industry averages, comparison of transaction factors (loan terms and conditions) to loan policy and comparison of credit history to stated repayment terms and industry averages. Some grading factors are necessarily
        more subjective such as economic and industry factors, regulatory environment and management. C&amp;I and CRE loans are graded Doubtful, Substandard, Special Mention and Pass.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73347" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73348"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e22" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e23">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73348" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73349"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e23" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e24">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Doubtful</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73349" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73350"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e24" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e25">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73350" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73351"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e25" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e26">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A Doubtful loan has a high probability of total or substantial loss, but because of specific pending events that may strengthen the asset, its
        classification as a loss is deferred. Doubtful borrowers are usually in default, lack adequate liquidity or capital and lack the resources necessary to remain an operating entity. Pending events can include mergers, acquisitions, liquidations,
        capital injections, the perfection of liens on additional collateral, the valuation of collateral and refinancing. Generally, pending events should be resolved within a relatively short period and the ratings will be adjusted based on the new
        information. Nonaccrual treatment is required for Doubtful assets because of the high probability of loss.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73351" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73352"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e26" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e27">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
        <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73352" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73353"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e27" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e28">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Substandard</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
        <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73353" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73354"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e28" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e29">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
        <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73354" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73355"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e29" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e30">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Substandard loans have a high probability of payment default or they have other well-defined weaknesses. They require more intensive supervision
          by bank management. Substandard loans are generally characterized by current or expected unprofitable operations, inadequate debt service coverage, inadequate liquidity or marginal capitalization. Repayment may depend on collateral or other
          credit risk mitigants. For some Substandard loans, the likelihood of full collection of interest and principal may be in doubt and those loans should be placed on nonaccrual. Although Substandard assets in the aggregate will have a distinct
          potential for loss, an individual asset&#8217;s loss potential does not have to be distinct for the asset to be rated Substandard.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      </div>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73355" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73356"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e30" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e31">
<div style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73356" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73357"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e31" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e32">
<div style="text-align: left; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Special Mention</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73357" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73358"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e32" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e33">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73358" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73359"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e33" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e34">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Special Mention loans have potential weaknesses that may, if not checked or corrected, weaken the asset or inadequately protect the Company&#8217;s
        position at some future date. These loans pose elevated risk, but their weakness does not yet justify a Substandard classification. Borrowers may be experiencing adverse operating trends (i.e., declining revenues or margins) or may be struggling
        with an ill-proportioned balance sheet (i.e., increasing inventory without an increase in sales, high leverage and/or tight liquidity). Adverse economic or market conditions, such as interest rate increases or the entry of a new competitor, may
        also support a Special Mention rating. Although a Special Mention loan has a higher PD than a Pass asset, its default is not imminent.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73359" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73360"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e34" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e35">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73360" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73361"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e35" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e36">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Pass</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73361" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73362"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e36" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e37">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73362" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73363"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e37" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e38">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans graded as Pass encompass all loans not graded as Doubtful, Substandard or Special Mention.&#160;Pass loans are in compliance with loan covenants
        and payments are generally made as agreed.&#160;Pass loans range from superior quality to fair quality. Pass loans also include any portion of a government guaranteed loan, including Paycheck Protection Program loans.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73363" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73364"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e38" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e39">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73364" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73365"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e39" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e40">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Consumer and Residential Grading System</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73365" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73366"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e40" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e41">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73366" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73367"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e41" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e42">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Consumer and Residential loans are graded as either Nonperforming or Performing.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73367" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73368"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e42" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e43">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73368" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73369"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e43" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e44">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Nonperforming</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73369" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73370"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e44" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e45">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73370" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73371"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e45" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e46">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Nonperforming loans are loans that are (1) over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:ThresholdPeriodPastDueForLoansToBeConsideredNonperforming" id="Fact_48724f67f17b49789d7d713be99bd1a8" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days past due and interest is still accruing or (2) on nonaccrual status.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73371" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73372"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e46" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e47">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73372" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73373"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e47" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e48">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Performing</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73373" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73374"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e48" continuedAt="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e49">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73374" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73375"><ix:continuation id="Text_df5ac07713b54b748953e0e154670b7e49">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">All loans not meeting any of the above criteria are considered Performing.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73375" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73376">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

      <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:LoanModificationsToBorrowersExperiencingFinancialDifficultiesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_1e8de88aab8e42d4a18051dd3e6392f7" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_b2660610f5bf41c4b357729ea57fa15a1"><ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73388" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73389">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Loan Modifications to Borrowers Experiencing Financial Difficulties</span><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
        <ix:continuation id="Text_b2660610f5bf41c4b357729ea57fa15a1"><ix:continuation id="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73389" continuedAt="Text_fd069f56b9ff4f9e93e8af92288dd73390">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
          </span>The Company&#8217;s January 1, 2023 adoption of ASU 2022-02 eliminates the recognition and measurement of TDRs. Upon adoption of this guidance, the Company no longer recognizes an allowance for credit losses for the economic concession granted
          to a borrower for changes in the timing and amount of contractual cash flows when a loan is restructured. The adoption of ASU 2022-02 resulted in a change to reporting for loan modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulties. With
          the adoption of ASU 2022-02 these modifications required enhanced reporting on the type of modifications granted and the financial magnitude of the concessions granted.<br/>
          <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
          </span>When the Company modifies a loan with financial difficulty, such modifications generally include one or a combination of the following: an extension of the maturity date at a stated rate of interest lower than the current market rate for
          new debt with similar risk; a change in scheduled payment amount; or principal forgiveness.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      </div>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:LesseeOperatingLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_ff16d3f1e106419ebb4354cb58dd6a8e" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e1"><ix:continuation id="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd6607779" continuedAt="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077710">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Operating leases in which the Company is the lessee are recorded as operating lease ROU assets and operating lease liabilities, included in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_d02d42d2f18b441ab3286853c09fc369"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_7f9123246bcb4647bdc81bf654c947ee">other assets</span></span> and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_8a1d0e24e6634aa2ac0dc3edb17b25b2"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_3cc8364deb774580a60c2e51f8c8e32a">other liabilities</span></span>,
      respectively, on the consolidated balance sheets. The Company does not have any significant finance leases in which we are the lessee as of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e1" continuedAt="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e2"><ix:continuation id="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077710" continuedAt="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077711">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e2" continuedAt="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e3"><ix:continuation id="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077711" continuedAt="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077712">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Operating lease ROU assets represent the Company&#8217;s right to use an underlying asset during the lease term and operating lease liabilities represent
      our obligation to make lease payments arising from the lease. ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are recognized at lease commencement based on the present value of the remaining lease payments using a discount rate that represents the
      Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate at the lease commencement date. ROU assets are further adjusted for lease incentives. Operating lease expense, which is comprised of amortization of the ROU asset and the implicit interest accreted on the
      operating lease liability, is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and is recorded in occupancy expense in the consolidated statements of income.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e3" continuedAt="Text_29a7256e1aa84f13aa01ada0943ea83e4"><ix:continuation id="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077712" continuedAt="Text_7acde0413e5141eeba372cdbbd66077713">

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company made a policy election to exclude the recognition requirements to all classes of leases with original terms of 12 months or less.
      Instead, the short-term lease payments are recognized in profit or loss on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</div>

          business trusts, CNBF Capital Trust I, NBT Statutory Trust I, NBT Statutory Trust II, Alliance Financial Capital Trust I and Alliance Financial Capital Trust II (collectively, the &#8220;Trusts&#8221;). The Company&#8217;s junior subordinated debentures include
          amounts related to the Company&#8217;s NBT Statutory Trust I and II as well as junior subordinated debentures associated with <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:NumberOfStatutoryBusinessTrusts" id="Fact_a5a996d0ac494b5d964d17aaacc60ae5" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_DebtInstrumentAxis_CnbfCapitalTrustIDebentureMember" unitRef="U012" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> statutory
          trust affiliate that was acquired from our merger with CNB Financial Corp. and <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:NumberOfStatutoryBusinessTrusts" id="Fact_150cce1bbad249959aeb87551bef7d45" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_LegalEntityAxis_AllianceFinancialCapitalMember" unitRef="U012" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> statutory trusts that were acquired from our
          acquisition of Alliance Financial Corporation (&#8220;Alliance&#8221;). The Trusts were formed for the purpose of issuing company-obligated mandatorily redeemable trust preferred securities to third-party investors and investing in the proceeds from the sale
          of such preferred securities solely in junior subordinated debt securities of the Company for general corporate purposes. The Company guarantees, on a limited basis, payments of distributions on the trust preferred securities and payments on
          redemption of the trust preferred securities. The Trusts are VIEs for which the Company is not the primary beneficiary, as defined by GAAP. In accordance with GAAP, the accounts of the Trusts are not included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated
          financial statements. See Note 1 for additional information about the Company&#8217;s consolidation policy.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s junior subordinated debentures are redeemable prior to the maturity date at our option upon each trust&#8217;s stated option repurchase
          dates and from time to time thereafter. These debentures are also redeemable in whole at any time upon the occurrence of specific events defined within the trust indenture. Our obligations under the debentures and related documents, taken
          together, constitute a full and unconditional guarantee by the Company of the issuers&#8217; obligations under the trust preferred securities. The Company owns all of the common stock of the Trusts, which have issued trust preferred securities in
          conjunction with the Company issuing trust preferred debentures to the Trusts. The terms of the trust preferred debentures are substantially the same as the terms of the trust preferred securities.</div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">With respect to the Trusts, the Company has the right to defer payments of interest on the debentures issued to the Trusts at any time or from
          time to time for a period of up to <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DistributionDeferralPeriodSubordinatedDebentures" id="Fact_450dae078fb94ac3b0492e969c17d3c7" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_LegalEntityAxis_CombinedTrustsMember" unitRef="U013" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">ten</ix:nonFraction> consecutive semi-annual periods with respect to each deferral period. Under the terms of the
          debentures, if in certain circumstances there is an event of default under the debentures or the Company elects to defer interest on the debentures, the Company may not, with certain exceptions, declare or pay any dividends or distributions on
          its capital stock or purchase or acquire any of its capital stock.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Despite the fact that the Trusts are not included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:TrustPreferredSecuritiesIncludedTierOneCapital" id="Fact_1ef695cfadc446aeb348610a63dfa011" contextRef="c20241231_LegalEntityAxis_CombinedTrustsMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">97</ix:nonFraction> million of the $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DebtInstrumentAmountOwedToTrust" id="Fact_26d4f79bce5449f5a4d7d6413878ec9e" contextRef="c20241231_LegalEntityAxis_CombinedTrustsMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">101</ix:nonFraction> million in trust preferred securities
          issued by these subsidiary trusts is included in the Tier 1 capital of the Company for regulatory capital purposes as allowed by the FRB (NBT Bank owns $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestments" id="Fact_afc9ed85aacf4f168d0be909115ddecc" contextRef="c20241231_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_ParentCompanyMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.0</ix:nonFraction>
          million of CNBF Trust I securities). The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010 requires bank holding companies with assets greater than $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:MinimumAssetsForBankHoldingCompaniesToBeSubjectToSameCapitalRequirementsAsInsuredDepositoryInstitutions" id="Fact_f0ea73c5659442ceb843511302091e01" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">500</ix:nonFraction> million to be subject to the same capital requirements as insured depository institutions, meaning, for instance, that such bank holding companies will not be able to count trust
          preferred securities issued after May 19, 2010 as Tier 1 capital. The aforementioned Trusts are grandfathered with respect to this enactment based on their date of issuance.</div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income.&#160;A valuation allowance is recorded when it is more likely than not that
        some portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized.&#160;Based on available evidence, gross deferred tax assets will ultimately be realized and a valuation allowance was not deemed necessary at December 31, 2024 and 2023.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">12.</span>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Employee Benefit Plans</span></div>

<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Defined Benefit Post-Retirement Plans</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf74" continuedAt="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf75"><ix:continuation id="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc851" continuedAt="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc852">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf75" continuedAt="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf76"><ix:continuation id="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc852" continuedAt="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc853">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has a qualified, noncontributory, defined benefit pension plan (&#8220;the Plan&#8221;) covering substantially all of its employees at December 31, 2024. Benefits paid
      from the Plan are based on age, years of service, compensation and social security benefits and are determined in accordance with defined formulas. The Company&#8217;s policy is to fund the Plan in accordance with Employee Retirement Income Security Act of
      1974 standards. Assets of the Plan are invested in publicly traded stocks, bonds and mutual funds. Prior to January 1, 2000, the Plan was a traditional defined benefit plan based on final average compensation.&#160;On January 1, 2000, the Plan was
      converted to a cash balance plan with grandfathering provisions for existing participants. Effective March 1, 2013, the Plan was amended.&#160;Benefit accruals for participants who, as of January 1, 2000, elected to continue participating in the
      traditional defined benefit plan design were frozen as of March 1, 2013.&#160;In May 2013, the noncontributory, frozen, defined benefit pension plan assumed from Alliance in the acquisition was merged into the Plan. In addition to the Plan, the Company
      provides supplemental employee retirement plans to certain current and former executives.&#160;The Company also assumed supplemental retirement plans for former executives in the Alliance acquisition. These supplemental employee retirement plans and the
      Plan are collectively referred to herein as &#8220;Pension Benefits.&#8221;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf76" continuedAt="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf77"><ix:continuation id="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc853" continuedAt="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc854">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In addition, the Company provides certain health care benefits for retired employees. Benefits were accrued over the employees&#8217; active service period. Only employees
      that were employed by the Company on or before January 1, 2000 are eligible to receive post-retirement health care benefits.&#160;The Plan is contributory for participating retirees, requiring participants to absorb certain deductibles and coinsurance
      amounts with contributions adjusted annually to reflect cost sharing provisions and benefit limitations called for in the Plan. Employees become eligible for these benefits if they reach normal retirement age while working for the Company.&#160;For
      eligible employees described above, the Company funds the cost of post-retirement health care as benefits are paid. The Company elected to recognize the transition obligation on a delayed basis over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:TransitionObligationPeriodOfRecognition" id="Fact_940de75966374cad8ffb244327b494de" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">twenty years</ix:nonNumeric>.&#160;In addition, the Company assumed post-retirement medical life insurance benefits for certain Alliance employees, retirees and their spouses, if applicable, in the
      Alliance acquisition.&#160;These post-retirement benefits are referred to herein as &#8220;Other Benefits.&#8221;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf78" continuedAt="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf79"><ix:continuation id="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc855" continuedAt="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc856">

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Accounting standards require an employer to: (1) recognize the overfunded or underfunded status of defined benefit post-retirement plans, which is
      measured as the difference between plan assets at fair value and the benefit obligation, as an asset or liability in its balance sheet; (2) recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur through comprehensive income;
      and (3) measure the defined benefit plan assets and obligations as of the date of its year-end balance sheet.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s key investment objectives in managing its defined benefit plan assets are to ensure that present and future benefit obligations to all participants and
      beneficiaries are met as they become due; to provide a total return that, over the long-term, maximizes the ratio of the plan assets to liabilities, while minimizing the present value of required Company contributions, at the appropriate levels of
      risk; to meet statutory requirements and regulatory agencies&#8217; requirements; and to satisfy applicable accounting standards.&#160;The Company periodically evaluates the asset allocations, funded status, rate of return assumption and contribution strategy
      for satisfaction of our investment objectives.&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Determination of Assumed Rate of Return</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf760" continuedAt="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf761"><ix:continuation id="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc8513" continuedAt="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc8514">
<div style="text-align: justify;"><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf761" continuedAt="Text_8b97d0c5fa4b4d4a9b1567ce786f3cf762"><ix:continuation id="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc8514" continuedAt="Text_db3e8ff897b7414ebb9f7b60f439bc8515">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The expected long-term rate-of-return on assets was <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationExpectedLongTermReturnOnPlanAssets" id="Fact_45c7d042a1f34077846244214fda3761" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U005" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationExpectedLongTermReturnOnPlanAssets" id="Fact_32023983692044bab91996f8f8f51778" contextRef="c20231231" unitRef="U005" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">6.7</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>%
      at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.&#160;This assumption represents the rate of return on plan assets reflecting the average rate of earnings expected on the funds invested or to be invested to provide for the benefits included in the projected
      benefit obligation.&#160;The assumption has been determined by reflecting expectations regarding future rates of return for the portfolio considering the asset distribution and related historical rates of return.&#160;The appropriateness of the assumption is
      reviewed annually.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In May 2024, the Company adopted the NBT Bancorp Inc. 2024 Omnibus Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Stock Plan&#8221;) replacing the 2018 Omnibus Incentive Plan. Under the terms of the
      Stock Plan, equity-based awards are granted to directors and employees to increase their direct proprietary interest in the operations and success of the Company.&#160;The Stock Plan assumed all prior equity-based incentive plans and any new equity-based
      awards are granted under the terms of the Stock Plan.&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Restricted shares granted under the Plan typically vest after </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_1e19598e7e1944a3b654a788e982611b">three</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> or </span><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" id="Fact_69ef02f628464eab94314e7eb0cf62ac" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_AwardTypeAxis_RestrictedStockMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis_EmployeesMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric> for employees and <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" id="Fact_fe538e580c32401a8a442427cbd99c8f" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_AwardTypeAxis_RestrictedStockMember_RangeAxis_MinimumMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis_DirectorMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> for non-employee directors. Restricted
      stock units granted under the Stock Plan may have different terms and conditions.&#160;Performance shares and units granted under the Stock Plan for executives may have different terms and conditions. Since 2011, the Company primarily grants restricted
      stock unit awards. Stock option grants since that time were reloads of existing grants which terminate <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:StockAwardsTerminationPeriod" id="Fact_1aba97260a1147c1a76ad1f4d5451d76" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_AwardTypeAxis_EmployeeStockOptionMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ten years</ix:nonNumeric> from the date of the <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">grant. <span style="font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Under
          terms of the Stock Plan, stock options are granted to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at a price equal to the fair market value of the common stock on the date of the grant. Shares issued as a result of vesting of restricted stock
          unit awards and stock option exercises are funded from the Company&#8217;s treasury stoc</span>k.</span></div>

      was available for payment of dividends to the Company without approval by the OCC. The Bank&#8217;s ability to pay dividends also is subject to the Bank being in compliance with regulatory capital requirements.&#160;The Bank is currently in compliance with
      these requirements. Under the State of Delaware General Corporation Law, the Company may declare and pay dividends either out of accumulated net retained earnings or capital surplus.</div>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" id="Text_89c9b9dd10e542fe8cb7594fca20c8d4" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf1">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">15.</span>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Regulatory Capital Requirements</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf1" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf2"><hr style="height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; text-align: center; border: none; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"/></ix:continuation></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf2" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf3">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf3" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf4">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company and the Bank are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies.&#160;Failure to meet minimum capital
      requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the consolidated financial statements. Under capital adequacy guidelines and the
      regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of NBT Bank&#8217;s assets, liabilities and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting
      practices. The capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings and other factors.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf4" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf5">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf5" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf6">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Company and the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the
      table below) of total and Tier 1 Capital to risk-weighted assets and of Tier 1 capital to average assets. <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">In addition to maintaining minimum capital ratios, the
        Company is subject to a capital conservation buffer (&#8220;Buffer&#8221;) of 2.50% above the minimum to avoid restriction on capital distributions and discretionary bonus paychecks to officers. At&#160;</span>December 31, 2024<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">&#160;and&#160;</span>2023, the Company and the Bank meet all capital adequacy requirements to which they were subject.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf6" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf7">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf7" continuedAt="Text_bd501e59d0a840168c79177791e885cf8">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Under their prompt corrective action regulations, regulatory authorities are required to take certain supervisory actions (and may take additional discretionary actions)
      with respect to an undercapitalized institution. Such actions could have a direct material effect on an institution&#8217;s financial statements.&#160;The regulations establish a framework for the classification of banks into five categories:&#160;well-capitalized,
      adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized and critically undercapitalized. As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the most recent notifications from the Bank&#8217;s regulators categorized the Bank as well-capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt
      corrective action.&#160;To be categorized as well-capitalized the Bank must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier 1 risk-based and Tier 1 Capital to Average Asset ratios as set forth in the table below. There are no conditions or events since that
      notification that management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s category.</div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In March 2020, the OCC, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) announced an interim final rule
          to delay the estimated impact on regulatory capital stemming from the implementation of CECL. Under the modified CECL transition provision, the regulatory capital impact of the January 1, 2020 CECL adoption date adjustment to the allowance for
          credit losses (after-tax) has been deferred and will phase into regulatory capital at 25% per year commencing January 1, 2022. For the ongoing impact of CECL, the Company was allowed to defer the regulatory capital impact of the allowance for
          credit losses in an amount equal to 25% of the change in the allowance for credit losses (pre-tax) recognized through earnings for each period between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021. The cumulative adjustment to the allowance for credit
          losses between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021, will also phase into regulatory capital at 25% per year commencing January 1, 2022.<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> The Company adopted the
            capital transition relief over the permissible </span><ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:PermissibleCapitalTransitionReliefPeriod" id="Fact_175a04d6022c4ee7b4d6a2236c9d8999" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five-year</ix:nonNumeric><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> period</span>. </div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December 31, 2024, approximately <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:PercentageOfCompanysLoansSecuredByRealEstate" id="Fact_23d76ca252ff43a1b2906c0e6b2f3938" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">64</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s

      substantial portion of the Company&#8217;s portfolio is susceptible to changes in market conditions of those areas. Management is not aware of any material concentrations of credit to any industry or individual borrowers.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6f51b2b779314da799920a4b586dbba16" continuedAt="Text_6f51b2b779314da799920a4b586dbba17">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_6f51b2b779314da799920a4b586dbba17" continuedAt="Text_6f51b2b779314da799920a4b586dbba18"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfGuaranteeObligationsTextBlock" id="Text_85d1e22907a4435285fa1d93d9c8ebb2" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_bf77e773c5134fadb4ab2f018e11c7cb1">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is a party to certain financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These
      financial instruments include commitments to extend credit, unused lines of credit, standby letters of credit and certain agricultural real estate loans sold to investors with recourse, with the sold portion having a government guarantee that is
      assignable back to the Company upon repurchase of the loan in the event of default. The Company&#8217;s exposure to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the commitments to extend credit, unused lines of credit, standby letters
      of credit and loans sold with recourse is represented by the contractual amount of those instruments. The credit risk associated with commitments to extend credit and standby and commercial letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved
      with extending loans to customers and is subject to normal credit policies.&#160;Collateral may be obtained based on management&#8217;s assessment of the customer&#8217;s creditworthiness.&#160;</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

      are not necessarily indicative of future cash flows. The Company does not issue any guarantees that would require liability-recognition or disclosure, other than its standby letters of credit.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company guarantees the obligations or performance of customers by issuing standby letters of credit to third-parties. These standby letters of
      credit are generally issued in support of third-party debt, such as corporate debt issuances, industrial revenue bonds and municipal securities. The risk involved in issuing standby letters of credit is essentially the same as the credit risk
      involved in extending loan facilities to customers and letters of credit are subject to the same credit origination, portfolio maintenance and management procedures in effect to monitor other credit and off-balance sheet products. Typically, these
      instruments have <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:GuarantorObligationsPeriod" id="Fact_435d9ff730dd4dd6be080326c0353396" contextRef="c20240101to20241231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> expirations with an option to renew upon annual review; therefore, the total amounts do not necessarily
      represent future cash requirements. As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the fair value of the Company&#8217;s standby letters of credit was not significant.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6f51b2b779314da799920a4b586dbba114" continuedAt="Text_6f51b2b779314da799920a4b586dbba115">

    </div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In the normal course of business there are various outstanding legal proceedings. If legal costs are deemed material by management, the Company accrues for the estimated
      loss from a loss contingency if the information available indicates that it is probable that a liability had been incurred at the date of the financial statements and the amount of loss can be reasonably estimated.</div>
</ix:continuation>
